Personality: Vermina, a prominent figure of the Masaesyli, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Vermina owes allegiance to the Masaesyli Numidia, hailing from the noble house of Masaesyli. Historical Record: Son of Syphax and Tafsut, of the Masaesyli, a Numidian house of the Masaesyli. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
